section_summary: This section continues the March 1941 issue of the Spanish-language magazine Oriente y Occidente, combining Japanese cultural diplomacy and promotional material with Argentine literary, artistic, and historical writing. Major pieces defend Japanese culture and modernization, criticize alleged United States imperialism, and describe Japanese music, art, tourism, medicine, industry, cinema, religion, and life in Manchukuo. The issue also includes Argentine essays, poems, art criticism, and a colonial document concerning a 1702 dispute over abstinence from meat in Córdoba; the final article continues beyond page 206.

subfiles.title: Oriente y Occidente, March 1941, internal pages 15–61 (continuation)
subfiles.about: A continuation of a Buenos Aires magazine issue presenting Japanese cultural and economic publicity alongside Argentine essays, poetry, art criticism, and historical material.
subfiles.summary: The excerpt opens with Argentine political and artistic commentary, followed by a sustained critique of United States imperialism and a long account of the purportedly national and socially integrated character of Japanese culture. Numerous shorter features promote Japanese music, medicine, education, tourism, industry, cinema, silk production, and life in Manchukuo, while literary pages discuss Roussel and Rimbaud, publish poetry and haiku, and reproduce a Buddhist sermon. Argentine subjects include Chaco sculpture, Georgina Villanueva de Krause’s painting, Esteban Echeverría, Alfonsina Storni, and colonial social history. The last article reproduces a 1702 Córdoba petition seeking exemptions from Lenten abstinence and continues beyond page 206.
